If half of the Mississippi river's drainage basin was covered with bogs and mires, how would this affect the water and water level fluctuations of the river?

It would probably depend. In the winter and early spring, the ground is usually frozen, so the water doesn't seep into the ground much anyways. Additionally, a lot of "wild" rivers tend to have bends that migrate over time, so an area of bog may become an area of river more easily than a dryer area.

Lastly, whether an area is a bog, marsh, swamp, mire, etc depends on lot on elevation, as that area tends to have at least mud puddles for the entire year if not a measurable liquid level. An area half the size of the Mississippi river basin would require half of the midwest to be flat and level.

Story time! For the last 15 or so years, my Dad has been seeing this doctor he was not over fond of. He is a combat veteran with associated medical conditions, receiving disability pay from the VA.

He recently switched to a new doctor. After reviewing his medical records, this new doc informed him that he was suffering from degenerative joint disease (for about 10 years) and that he had two mildly serious heart conditions (also going back at least 10 years). So, the old doctor had known about these things and documented them, but never informed or treated my Dad of/for them.

The heart conditions are likely connected to his time in combat, and if he had known about them, he would have been receiving more disability from the VA, amounting to a little over 170k over the last 10 years.

The joint disease, since it went untreated, will almost definitely result in a knee replacement surgery later this year.

So the main question is, would there be a case? Is it worth pursuing? My mom's main argument against suing is "it's not right" but I think it's not right for the doctor to get away with not doing her job. They could really have used the extra 17k per year over the last 10 years, and they could still really use it now.

Also worth mentioning that they do not have the funds to hire a lawyer right now. I have heard in the past that some lawyers will take cases for a percentage of the winnings -- is this case clear enough for that to be an option?

You can consult several attorneys (for free) and ask them if they believe you have a case.

Understandably, you'd need a lot of documentation (which requires your father's authorization, since it is 'protected health info') to prove his claim ...

Make sure to to confirm it is a free consultation before you go or spend an hour on the phone with them. It should be your first question then get assurance that anything you discuss is privileged. Some jerk may try to bill you for time if you don't.

Most cases like this are paid for by the law firm - they spend a LOT of money on you - but they get like 1/3 to 1/2 of your winnings. If you want all the winnings you pay for the case in advance, and then they are not as motivated to win!

Yes go and talk to an attorney. But leave nothing out after you tell them you are talking to them as a client.

Realize that every "relevant" part of your Dad's life will come out and be discussed by strangers. Realize some attorneys will tell you to fuck off because you are looking at 100k-$2m in damages (maybe) and they want $20 million cases only.

Get all his medical records, NEVER lie to your attorney and shop around! Talk to many attorneys.

There is no way for me to know if you have a case without access to lots of details. Get those details ready, go in there, and be honest.

Tell the attorney you think your Dad will suffer incredibly in pain and suffering because of the negligence of the previous doctor. Tell them there is room for punitive damages on top - although they should be thinking this.

Actually I know a great business law firm in Massachusetts. I could give you a number and they could refer you to who is serious about insurance suits there. Just don't embarrass me OP if you have failed to mention something like your dad did crystal meth to deal with the PTSD from being a vet - DO NOT leave something like this out they will find out!!

Anyway reply or PM if you are serious and get your facts and dates together - the number I give you is a major business/contracts firm that happens to have an office where you are, they will know who has the reputation to bring the fire up there and make a defendant nervous in insurance cases (malpractice).

Be prepared to be referred around. Your $2M case may not be big enough, so the third office you speak to may be the one you visit. Just do not lie - I don't know how much to emphasize this. DO NOT LIE.

Also - expect that your case will settle for some amount out of court, this is reasonable, it is highly unlikely you will go to trial.
